# Content review

Every factual claim in the lessons, for locator sign-off.

- **How to sign off:** add the claim to `content/review/signoffs.json` with the hash shown, your initials and the date. Or send the IDs and we'll add them.
- **Edited claims:** editing a claim changes its hash and puts it back in review.

**State-specific claims:** none so far. The lessons teach no state rules.

**Sources:** the Source column says where a claim comes from, from these:

- **APWA card:** [APWA Uniform Color Code: Guidelines for Uniform Temporary Marking of Underground Facilities (Rev. 4/99)](https://www.apwa.org/wp-content/uploads/Uniform-Color-Code-1.pdf), American Public Works Association.
- **CGA Best Practices:** [CGA Best Practices 22.0, Appendix B: Uniform Color Code and Marking Guidelines](https://www.bluestakes.org/pdfs/CGA_BestPractices_ApxB.pdf), Common Ground Alliance.
- **CGA glossary:** [CGA Best Practices 10.0, Glossary: Locator](https://www.georgia811.com/userfiles/file/PDF_libary/CGA_BestPractices.pdf), Common Ground Alliance.
- **PHMSA:** [PHMSA Recognizes April as National Safe Digging Month (April 12, 2022)](https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/news/phmsa-recognizes-april-national-safe-digging-month-0), Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration.
- **BLS:** [Surveyors, Occupational Outlook Handbook](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/architecture-and-engineering/surveyors.htm), U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.
- **FCC:** [47 CFR § 1.1402(i), the definition of conduit](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-47/chapter-I/subchapter-A/part-1/subpart-J/section-1.1402), Federal Communications Commission.
- **Merriam-Webster (conduit):** [Conduit](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/conduit), Merriam-Webster.
- **USGS glossary:** [Water Science Glossary: potable water, reclaimed wastewater](https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/water-science-glossary), U.S. Geological Survey, Water Science School.
- **Merriam-Webster (slurry):** [Slurry](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/slurry), Merriam-Webster.
- **USGS coal slurry study:** [Comparative assessment of water use and environmental implications of coal slurry pipelines (1977)](https://www.usgs.gov/publications/comparative-assessment-water-use-and-environmental-implications-coal-slurry-pipelines), U.S. Geological Survey.
- **The scene:** Describes the lesson’s own scene, not the world.
- **The game:** How the lesson’s game works.

## Signal model calibrations

Teaching values from `src/signal/constants.ts`. `docs/SIGNAL_MODEL.md` explains how they combine and lists the eight resulting states.

| ID | Calibration | Hash | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model.block-length` | Block length: 140 ft. Long enough to see the signal fade in the 3D view, short enough to show street detail. | `5d6de62c12` | Not reviewed |
| `model.model-length` | Model length: 500 ft. Well past the block, so the signal that continues beyond it is part of the model, and its return through the earth with it. | `24fdcd43ad` | Not reviewed |
| `model.fade-on-the-coated-steel-main` | Fade on the coated steel main: 512 Hz: 0.93, 8 kHz: 0.72, 33 kHz: 0.2, 83 kHz: 0.04 (share left per 100 ft). Higher frequencies leak through the pipe coating into the soil more easily, so they fade sooner and don't travel as far. Compressed so the difference shows within one block: real lines fade far more gradually, in the same order. | `20f05c463a` | Not reviewed |
| `model.fade-on-the-tracer-wire` | Fade on the tracer wire: 512 Hz: 0.95, 8 kHz: 0.8, 33 kHz: 0.5, 83 kHz: 0.19 (share left per 100 ft). The same trend as the steel main, compressed the same way. A thin insulated wire leaks less than the big coated main at every frequency. | `97e07655ea` | Not reviewed |
| `model.bleed-over-onto-the-telecom-cable` | Bleed-over onto the telecom cable: 512 Hz: 0.02, 8 kHz: 0.06, 33 kHz: 0.15, 83 kHz: 0.32 (share of target current). Coupling onto a metal line running alongside grows with frequency, so higher frequencies bleed over more. | `ccd098cb0b` | Not reviewed |
| `model.circuit-resistance-steel-main` | Circuit resistance, steel main: 512 Hz: 60, 8 kHz: 56, 33 kHz: 52, 83 kHz: 48 (Ω). A long metal main has many paths to the earth, so it is a good circuit at every frequency. Higher frequencies find a little more path through the soil. | `1828c0c654` | Not reviewed |
| `model.circuit-resistance-tracer-wire` | Circuit resistance, tracer wire: 512 Hz: 500, 8 kHz: 490, 33 kHz: 480, 83 kHz: 470 (Ω). An insulated tracer wire connects to the earth directly only where it is grounded, so its circuit has more resistance than a steel main and less current flows. Higher frequencies leak a little through the insulation, so the resistance falls slightly as frequency rises. | `d8d10c86a4` | Not reviewed |
| `model.transmitter-output` | Transmitter output: 50 V. An illustrative output that gives readings in a familiar range. | `c65cc44c24` | Not reviewed |
| `model.transmitter-internal-resistance` | Transmitter internal resistance: 50 Ω. Keeps the current on a good circuit in the hundreds of milliamps rather than unlimited. | `5e51402e08` | Not reviewed |
| `model.enough-signal-to-trace` | Enough signal to trace: 20 mA. An illustrative threshold. Real needs depend on depth, interference from other lines and noise, and the receiver. | `320fa40407` | Not reviewed |
